items.headline: U.S. Markets Close Mixed on Friday, October 24, 2026, as Tech Sector Faces Continued Headwinds.
items.summary: Major U.S. indices concluded Friday's trading session with mixed results. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 both experienced declines, while the Nasdaq Composite saw a modest dip, reflecting ongoing investor reassessment of AI-related investments and rising inflation worries. Defensive sectors showed resilience amidst broader market rotation. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Sector Rotation: Defensive Plays and Energy Lead as Tech Stumbles
items.summary: The past week, ending October 24, saw a notable rotation in equity markets. Investors pulled back from AI-related stocks, impacting semiconductor and tech-heavy indexes. Energy emerged as the top-performing sector, with defensive sectors like healthcare, utilities, and consumer staples also gaining ground and supporting broader market performance. Communication Services and Technology lagged.

items.headline: Q3 GDP Growth Stronger Than Expected; Inflation Worries Persist
items.summary: The first estimate for third-quarter GDP is expected to show an impressive 3.2% annualized gain, indicating robust economic momentum. However, inflation remains a concern, with the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report, the Fed's preferred measure, expected to show a 3.7% jump in September, up from 3.4% in August.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Poised to Hold Rates Amidst Upcoming Data
items.summary: The Federal Reserve is expected to conclude its upcoming two-day meeting (next Wednesday, October 28) by holding its benchmark interest rate steady, following a September hike. However, Wall Street anticipates another rate hike in December as the central bank continues to grapple with persistent inflation.

items.headline: Q3 Earnings Season Underway with Strong Beats; Key Tech Reports Awaited
items.summary: The third-quarter earnings season is progressing, with over 80% of S&P 500 companies that have reported beating consensus expectations so far. United Bankshares ($UBSI) reported strong Q3 earnings driven by record net interest income. However, earnings reports from Tesla and Meta rekindled concerns about AI investment spending. Next week will bring a wave of major Q3 earnings from companies including Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Boeing, Seagate, Corning, and Exxon Mobil.

items.headline: Geopolitical Tensions Drive Oil Prices Higher
items.summary: Rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East continued to push oil prices higher, with Brent crude climbing above $117 and WTI crude topping $100 a barrel. This surge in oil prices is contributing to ongoing inflation concerns.
